title: Probate vs letters of administration - when each is actually required
p1:
Many people think probate and letters of administration are the same thing.

They are not — and choosing the wrong one can delay the process of handling someone’s estate.
p2:
The surprising part? The difference usually comes down to one question: did the person who passed away leave a valid will?

Probate is generally needed when there is a will and the named executor needs legal authority to manage the estate. Letters of administration are usually needed when there is no valid will, so the court appoints someone to handle the estate instead.
p3:
A simple way to remember it: a will usually points to probate, while no will often leads to letters of administration.

This matters because the person who can access assets, settle debts, and distribute property may depend on getting the correct legal authority first.

Before assuming the process, check whether a valid will exists and who has the right to apply.
conclusion: Did you know the existence of a will can completely change whether probate or letters of administration is required? Which one surprised you more?
